name: Kaliningrad (Baltiysk) bottle-post cryptogram, found 2015
ciphertext_pending: Resolved 25 Sept 2026: full transcript found already on the saved post (Thomas Ernst, comment #32) and checked against the two fetched images; see ciphers/kaliningrad-2015/NOTES.md and cheap_test_done below.
alphabet: Latin letters with apostrophes and diacritics, 37 signs

constraints.apostrophes: after 11 letters, inside words: consistent with Russian soft/hard signs transliterated (Ernst in comments) or with Czech/Polish diacritics

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Get the full transcription from the Russian thread (one fetch) and the two images (two fetches); two-pass check of the transcription. Cost $2, Sonnet.

2. MASC anneal with the apostrophe as a modifier (letter+') vs as a separate sign, in transliterated Russian (fetch one Russian Gutenberg text and transliterate), Polish, Lithuanian and German; judge with the matching corpus; control per language at the same N and K. The IC of 0.054 already argues against a single-alphabet substitution of plain text in most of these (Russian ~0.055 is the closest, so Russian first). Cost $4, Sonnet.
3. If flat after 2: periodic IC for a short key. Cost under $1.
matched_control: same N and K in each candidate language

judge.note: Russian/Polish corpora are not on disk; add them as 'corpora' when fetched

value: moderate; 58 reader comments without a solution, but no machine run across the candidate languages is on record
status_24_Sept_2026: open per Schmeh 2017; nothing later found 24 Sept 2026

cheap_test_done.method: Fetched both cryptogram images from scienceblogs.de; used the full transcript already on the saved post (Thomas Ernst, comment #32, not the separate Russian dirty.ru thread, which was not fetched once the on-page transcript was found) as ciphertext.txt; checked it row by row against the images (own pass, spot-check resolution, not a second blind reconciled pass); computed N/K/IC and matched-N IC controls for transliterated Russian (one Gutenberg fetch, id 30774) and German (tools/data/de16).
cheap_test_done.control: ru (transliterated, Gutenberg 30774): IC mean=0.0563 range=(0.0543-0.0605), 20 windows N=978, seed 42; de (tools/data/de16/composed_enhg.txt): IC mean=0.0724 range=(0.0676-0.0765), 20 windows N=978 from a 6855-letter corpus (heavily overlapping, not independent), seed 42; Polish not fetched (one-Gutenberg-fetch budget spent on Russian)
cheap_test_done.verdict: not conclusive for language: target IC sits above the Russian control's range and near/inside the German control's range, which is not the direction a hard/soft-split K=36 alphabet would be expected to move IC if the plaintext really is one of these languages under simple substitution or transliteration. Row-level transcription check found no disagreement beyond a known labelling convention (Ernst's 'x' for the hard-sign-like glyph).
